concepts.label: Controlled execution
concepts.summary: A production work substrate that makes consequential execution authorized, observable, interruptible, reconstructable and testable.

public.summary: A production work substrate that makes consequential execution authorized, observable, interruptible, reconstructable and testable.

concepts.label: Execution history
concepts.summary: A durable record of what happened during work so state, decisions and actions can be reconstructed later.

public.summary: A durable record of what happened during work so state, decisions and actions can be reconstructed later.

concepts.label: Protected data separation
concepts.summary: Separating orchestration visibility from broad access to protected business data and secrets.

concepts.label: Human-agent task equivalence
concepts.summary: Modeling work so the executor can move between an AI agent and a person without creating a separate exception process.

concepts.label: Replayable evaluation
concepts.summary: Using reconstructed historical execution state to evaluate models, prompts, policies and tools against past work.

concepts.label: Policy as code
concepts.summary: Representing authorization and policy decisions as explicit, reviewable rules rather than scattered application logic.

public.summary: Representing authorization and policy decisions as explicit, reviewable rules rather than scattered application logic.

concepts.label: Observability
concepts.summary: Structured traces, metrics and logs that make distributed execution inspectable without becoming the source of business truth itself.

concepts.label: Durable execution
concepts.summary: Execution whose workflow progress survives process failure, waits and restarts because durable state exists outside any one Worker process.

public.summary: A reliability pattern for long-running work where progress can survive interruptions instead of depending only on one running process.

concepts.label: Workflow Execution
concepts.summary: The durable Temporal unit representing one running workflow identity and its persisted progress over time.

concepts.label: Event History
concepts.summary: Temporal's append-only event record that represents Workflow Execution progress and supports state reconstruction.

concepts.label: Task Queue
concepts.summary: The Temporal dispatch boundary from which Worker Processes poll Workflow and Activity tasks for execution.

concepts.label: Worker Process
concepts.summary: A replaceable process that polls Temporal Task Queues and runs Workflow or Activity application code.

concepts.label: Activity Execution
concepts.summary: The Temporal boundary for side-effecting work that can interact with external systems and may be retried after failure.

concepts.label: Idempotency under retry
concepts.summary: Designing external effects so repeating a failed operation does not create unintended duplicate outcomes.

concepts.label: Policy decision / enforcement separation
concepts.summary: Separating the component that computes a policy decision from the component that owns and enforces the protected action.

concepts.label: Open Policy Agent (OPA)
concepts.summary: A general-purpose policy engine that evaluates declarative Rego policy and data against structured input and returns policy decisions to integrating applications.

concepts.label: Policy distribution
concepts.summary: Distributing versioned policy and supporting data to decision points on a lifecycle separate from application deployment.

concepts.label: ReAct loop
concepts.summary: An agent trajectory that interleaves language reasoning, environment actions and returned observations so each step can update the next decision.

concepts.label: Reasoning trace
concepts.summary: A language-space step used to compose task context, plans or interpretations without itself changing the external environment.

concepts.label: Observation grounding
concepts.summary: Using evidence returned by an external action or environment to update the context for subsequent reasoning and action selection.

concepts.label: Retrieval practice
concepts.summary: Attempting to produce learned material from memory so retrieval itself becomes part of learning rather than only a later assessment event.

concepts.label: Immediate performance / delayed retention gap
concepts.summary: The same learning method can improve performance shortly after study yet rank differently when memory is tested after a meaningful delay.

concepts.label: Metacognitive confidence gap
concepts.summary: A mismatch between how well a learner predicts future remembering and how much material is actually retrievable after a delay.

concepts.label: Reconciliation loop
concepts.summary: A continuing control loop that observes current state, compares it with desired state and performs bounded corrective actions to reduce the difference.

concepts.label: Desired state
concepts.summary: A declarative representation of what a managed system or resource should look like, kept separate from observed reality.

concepts.label: Observed state
concepts.summary: The controller's current view of what is actually true, used as feedback for deciding whether corrective action is required.

relations.rationale: Consequential work cannot be reconstructed or evaluated later without a durable history of execution.
Governed orchestration should not require broad access to protected data simply to observe or control work.
Production work needs a stable task model when execution moves between an agent and a human reviewer.
Explicit policy decisions make authorization boundaries reviewable and testable instead of implicit in application code.
Operators need structured telemetry to inspect execution health even when business evidence lives in a separate durable record.
Historical execution state becomes reusable evaluation material only when enough context can be reconstructed reliably.
Durability solves continuity of execution while controlled execution adds governance, authority, evidence and intervention around that work.

public.rationale: Durability addresses continuity of work; controlled execution additionally requires authority, evidence, intervention and other governance controls.

relations.rationale: Temporal realizes durable work as a persisted Workflow Execution rather than tying workflow state to one running process.
Persisted Event History is the record from which Workflow Execution progress can be reconstructed after Worker failure.
Worker Processes execute application code for the durable Workflow Execution while remaining replaceable executors.
Workers receive executable Workflow and Activity tasks by polling the configured Temporal Task Queue.
Workers execute Activity code as one of the main boundaries where Temporal applications interact with external systems.
Activity retries can repeat external work, so safe side effects require idempotent or otherwise duplicate-safe design.
Temporal Event History is a concrete implementation-level example of the broader execution-history concept used in production architecture.
Policy-as-code becomes operationally precise when the decision engine and the application that enforces the result are modeled as separate trust boundaries.
OPA is a concrete implementation of policy-as-code: Rego and policy data are evaluated outside scattered application conditionals to produce explicit decisions.
Using OPA correctly depends on understanding that OPA computes policy decisions while the integrating application remains responsible for enforcing them.
OPA can provide an explicit authorization/policy-decision primitive inside a broader controlled-execution substrate, but it is not the complete substrate by itself.
OPA bundles show how distributed decision points can receive policy and data on a lifecycle separate from the application binaries that enforce decisions.
ReAct adds explicit language reasoning steps that maintain plans, interpret observations and support later action choices.
The loop is grounded by observations returned from environment actions; without useful feedback it can continue or reformulate poorly.
ReAct explains how a model selects and updates actions, while controlled execution governs whether consequential actions are authorized, safely executed, reconstructed and verified.
The study's central retrieval-practice result is a crossover in which extra study helps immediate performance while prior retrieval helps delayed retention.
Repeated-study participants predicted stronger one-week memory despite later recalling less, showing that immediate fluency/confidence can misrepresent delayed retention.
A controller needs an explicit target state in order to know what condition it should converge toward.
Reconciliation requires feedback about current reality so the controller can determine whether corrective work is necessary.
